title: Session of 1st Presbyterian Church, Augusta, GA v. Savannah River Presbytery
disposition_detail: Both specifications were sustained: the SJC answered yes to whether the Presbytery erred under BCO 25-2 and BCO 24-6. The Presbytery's contrary findings that the Session erred by adding its BCO 24-6 recommendation and by dissolving official relationships, and its annulment of the Session's subsequent actions, were set aside in effect; the Session's original actions were reinstated. Remaining relief sought by the complaint was held moot. One member recorded a dissent; no dissent text is supplied.
first_summary: Savannah River Presbytery found that the Session of First Presbyterian Church, Augusta erred by adding a BCO 24-6 recommendation to a petition-called congregational meeting and by acting on the congregation's vote. The SJC sustained the Session's complaint, holding that BCO 25-2 and BCO 24-6 do not bar those actions, and reinstated the Session's actions. Other relief was moot. One member dissented.
summary: A presbytery annulled a session's actions after the session added to a petition-called congregational meeting a recommendation that the congregation invoke BCO 24-6 against eleven elders. The SJC sustained the session's complaint: BCO 25-2 permits a session to add agenda items, and BCO 24-6 does not require a member-initiated motion; the congregation's own 503–229 vote began the process. It reinstated the session's actions, declared remaining relief moot, and noted one recorded dissent; no dissent text appears.

evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 67–78: both issues answered yes. Lines 81–128: BCO 25-2 allows the Session to add agenda items; BCO 24-6 does not limit initiation to a member motion; higher courts must defer to a lower court's discretion absent clear violation. The Session's actions were reinstated and remaining relief held moot.
